chunks: Yunus narrated from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār who said:
Abū al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The lost one (mafqūd), his wealth is waited for (for four years), then it is distributed.'

key_terms.الْمَفْقُودُ: The lost one; a person whose whereabouts are unknown and who is presumed dead after a specific waiting period.
key_terms.يُتَرَبَّصُ: To wait for or hold in reserve, typically in a legal context regarding the confirmation of a status.
key_terms.يُقْسَمُ: It is distributed; refers to the division of the estate among heirs.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for the inheritance of a person with unknown whereabouts (mafqūd)?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the four-year waiting period for a 'mafqūd' (presumed dead) before inheritance distribution, a ruling distinct from the standard five-year period for missing persons in some other schools. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential approach to balancing the rights of heirs with the possibility of the individual's return, ensuring financial stability during the interim. This specific timeline reflects the practical application of uncertainty in inheritance law within the Ja'fari school.

en.hubeali: Yunus, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘The lost, one should wait with his wealth for four years, then distribute it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Yunus has narrated from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has narrated the following:
“Abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘The assets of a lost person must be kept for four years; then they are distributed.’”
